hints: Use the bounded range of the cosine function $-1 \le \cos 2x \le 1$.
Calculate the maximum value when $\cos 2x = 1$ and minimum value when $\cos 2x = -1$.
walkthrough: Recall the range of the cosine function: $-1 \le \cos 2x \le 1$.

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Functions: States greatest value $7$ and least value $-1$.

hints: The period of $y = 4\cos 2x + 3$ is $\frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi$, so the curve completes 2 full cycles in $[0, 2\pi]$.
Plot key points: starts at $(0, 7)$, reaches minimum $-1$ at $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x = \frac{3\pi}{2}$, and peaks at $7$ at $x = 0, \pi, 2\pi$.
walkthrough: Over the domain $0 \le x \le 2\pi$, sketch two complete cosine cycles:
Cycle 1 from $x=0$ to $x=\pi$: starts at $(0, 7)$, reaches minimum $(\pi/2, -1)$, and returns to maximum $(\pi, 7)$.
Cycle 2 from $x=\pi$ to $x=2\pi$: reaches minimum $(3\pi/2, -1)$, and ends at $(2\pi, 7)$.

ai_rubric.Graph Sketching: Sketches two full cosine cycles starting/ending at $(0,7)$ and $(2\pi,7)$ with maxima $7$ and minima $-1$.

hints: Consider the straight line $y = 2x - 1$: at $x = 0$, $y = -1$, and at $x = 2\pi \approx 6.28$, $y \approx 11.57$.
Count the number of times the line $y = 2x - 1$ intersects the oscillating cosine curve on your sketch.
walkthrough:
Consider the straight line $y = 2x - 1$ on the interval $0 \le x \le 2\pi$:
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad y = -1 \quad (\text{below } y = 7)$$
$$\text{At } x = 2\pi \approx 6.28: \quad y = 2(2\pi) - 1 \approx 11.57 \quad (\text{above } y = 7)$$

Since the line crosses the two oscillating cosine cycles, count the intersection points on the sketch:
$$\text{Number of solutions} = 3$$

ai_rubric.Graphical Solutions: Determines that the equation has $3$ solutions.
